native_code_policy.description: Every byte of machine code in the delivered library, archive and executable must be produced by the pinned Rust toolchain from Rust sources inside the submission.
native_code_policy.allowed_rust_dependencies: std, core and alloc only. No crates.io dependencies, no git dependencies, no vendored third-party crates, no build-script code generation from C sources.
forbidden_build_actions: compiling any C, C++, Objective-C, Objective-C++ or assembly translation unit
invoking cc/gcc/clang/c++/g++/clang++/as/cpp for anything other than the final Rust link step
linking any prebuilt object file, static archive or shared library that ships inside the submission
downloading, fetching or cloning anything at configure, build, install or run time
loading code at run time with dlopen/dlsym/LD_PRELOAD
spawning a helper process to perform parsing or rendering

forbidden_paths.description: Paths matching these patterns must not exist anywhere under the submission root except inside an out-of-source build directory produced by the build itself.
forbidden_paths.header_allowlist_note: src/cmark.h is the installed public ABI contract and must be retained. Every other .h file in State A is a private C header and must be gone. Generated headers (cmark_export.h, cmark_version.h) belong in the build directory or may be produced from a .in template.

environment_during_build.CC: a shim that fails on any compile action
environment_during_build.CXX: a shim that fails on any compile action
environment_during_build.note: The shim forwards link-only invocations to the real linker driver, so a Rust cdylib/binary still links. Any attempt to compile a C or C++ translation unit fails the build and the audit gate.

install_inventory.description: Required entries under the install prefix. 'shared' and 'static' list the entries specific to that configuration; 'common' is required by both.

forbidden_extra.description: The install tree must not contain a second implementation or a fallback engine.

abi_contract.visibility: Only the documented cmark_* entry points may be globally visible. No Rust std symbols, no rust_eh_personality, no __rust_alloc, no internal helper may be exported.
abi_contract.note: cmark_mem is a caller-visible struct of three function pointers (calloc, realloc, free) and must keep C layout. cmark_node/cmark_parser/cmark_iter are opaque to callers, so their internal layout is unconstrained.

behavioral_contract.reference: cmark 0.31.1 built from the pinned upstream C sources
surfaces: cmark(1) command line: all options, all five output formats, stdin and file inputs, multi-file concatenation, exit statuses and stderr text
libcmark C API: all 70 exported functions including error paths, NULL handling, custom allocators, streaming parser feeds, iterators and tree mutation
installed man pages, pkg-config metadata and CMake package files
behavioral_contract.note: Where State A has quirks or arguably wrong behavior, State B must reproduce the quirk. Compatibility is defined against the reference implementation, not against the CommonMark specification prose.

preserved_paths.description: These files define the public contract and must remain present with unchanged semantics.

removable_paths.description: State A material whose purpose disappears with the C implementation. Removing these is expected; keeping a Rust equivalent is also acceptable as long as no forbidden path or build action results.
